CausalChain: Tumor cells secrete EVs enriched with specific miRNAs, lipids, and proteins -> EVs are taken up by myeloid progenitor cells -> Alteration of transcription regulators (e.g., suppression of IRF8, activation of C/EBPβ) -> Skewed differentiation into either monocytic or granulocytic MDSCs -> Enhanced immunosuppressive environment in the tumor microenvironment -> Reduced efficacy of anti-tumor immune responses and immunotherapy
Hypothesis: Distinct tumor-derived EV cargos dictate the differentiation pathway of myeloid progenitors toward either monocytic or granulocytic MDSCs, thereby customizing the immune suppressive landscape of different tumors. Interrupting EV-mediated signaling or modulating its cargo may reprogram MDSC differentiation towards a more mature, immunostimulatory myeloid phenotype, enhancing the effectiveness of cancer immunotherapies.
Abstract: Recent insights into the role of myeloid‐derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) in tumor immune evasion have highlighted their heterogeneous origins and the diverse mechanisms through which they suppress anti‐tumor responses. Here, we propose that tumor‐derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) carry distinct molecular cargos—including specific miRNAs, lipids, and proteins—that differentially modulate myeloid progenitor cell fate by altering key transcriptional regulators (e.g., IRF8, C/EBPβ). This differential modulation may lead to the preferential expansion of either monocytic or granulocytic MDSC subsets depending on the tumor type. Such an EV‐mediated reprogramming of myelopoiesis could shape the tumor microenvironment in a manner that directly impacts the efficacy of immunotherapeutic interventions. We hypothesize that targeting the specific EV cargo or its uptake pathways may reorient myeloid differentiation towards mature, immunogenic myeloid cells, thereby mitigating MDSC‐mediated immunosuppression and improving patient responses to cancer immunotherapies.
